newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates close sharply higher.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates close sharply higher.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates ended sharply higher on Wednesday, soaring over eight percent on ever tightening liquidity during the peak of routine monthly payroll demand, dealers said
They said government auctions of state shares in the past few days have further squeezed liquidity.
The overnight interbank rate finished at 8.748 percent against Tuesday's 7.784 finish, well above the central bank's 5.0-5.5 percent target zone.
The 30-day commercial paper jumped to 8.75 percent from 8.00.
Banking system's accumulated reserve excess has showed a negative T$115.6 billion since the beginning of the current reserve period.

Dealers said the government's five-day auction of some 418 million shares in Chiao Tung Bank, which began on Monday, was expected to further siphon some T$30 billion in liquidity out of the banking system.
In the bond market, the benchmark 86/4 bond yield was at 6.14 percent against Tuesday's 6.16 percent.
